Scalp aplasia cutis and terminal limb reduction define Adams-Oliver syndrome; individual cardiac defects occur in 1/5 reported patients.

Abnormal patency of the eustachian tube; increased infection risk does not establish an infectious disease.

Disorder of the cornea.

Inherited PTH deficiency causes hypocalcemia and hyperphosphatemia. Nephrocalcinosis is usually treatment-related; hypocalcemic seizures do not establish lasting brain damage.
Frontotemporal neuronal degeneration with tau-containing Pick bodies causes dementia.
Vertebral or PICA vascular occlusion produces lateral medullary infarction; dysphagia reflects brainstem injury rather than gastrointestinal damage.
Malignant tumour arising in the sublingual salivary gland.

Glioma susceptibility denotes inherited risk rather than an existing tumour or established organ injury; no currently affected organ is specified.
Lymphoid malignancy occupying the retroperitoneal space; retroperitoneal location alone does not establish renal or gastrointestinal invasion.
Prostatic malacoplakia with abscess is an infection-associated inflammatory disorder; prostate and seminal vesicles have no anatomical axis here.
Testicular germ cell malignancy; reproductive tumour origin has no axis, and endocrine dysfunction is not defining.
Inherited sensorineural hearing loss with vestibular dysfunction; both affect the inner ear.
Neuroendocrine tumour arising in the lung; neuroendocrine differentiation alone does not establish an endocrine disorder.
Malignant neoplasm involving the small intestine; lymphoma is only one subtype of this umbrella.
Platelet dense-granule deficiency and oculocutaneous albinism define HPS11, with reduced visual acuity. Pulmonary fibrosis and colitis are not established common features.
Delayed anoxic brain injury following carbon monoxide poisoning.
Primary disorder of ocular alignment; no systemic muscle or neurologic disease is specified.
Age-related degeneration of the peripheral retina.
